Barcode Rank ("Knee") Plots from Raw 10x Matrices

Source: R/plotBarcodeRanks.R
plotBarcodeRanks.Rd

Draws the standard barcode rank plot for one or more Cell Ranger runs: total UMI count against barcode rank on log-log axes, with the knee and inflection points DropletUtils::barcodeRanks() identifies (and, with older DropletUtils, the spline it fitted to find them). Takes the same manifest / path / multi arguments as seuratFrom10x(), and returns both the plotted curve and the figure for every run.

Usage

plotBarcodeRanks(
  manifest = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  multi = NULL,
  lower = 100,
  outdir = NULL,
  width = 6.5,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300,
  ...,
  multiplexed = NULL
)

Arguments

manifest

Data frame with columns Path (character; path to each run's outs/ directory) and multi (logical). Rows may mix the two pipelines freely. Mutually exclusive with path.

path

Character string. Path to a single Cell Ranger outs/ directory. Mutually exclusive with manifest.

multi

Logical. Whether path was produced by cellranger multi rather than cellranger count – see the section above. Required when path is supplied; ignored when manifest is supplied, since the pipeline is read per-row from manifest$multi instead.

lower

Total UMI count at or below which a barcode is assumed to be empty. DropletUtils::barcodeRanks() only looks above it when finding the knee and inflection; it does not filter the curve, and barcodes below it are still plotted. Default 100.

outdir

Directory to write a CSV of the curve and a PNG of the figure for each run, named <run>_barcode_ranks.csv / .png. Created if it does not exist. NULL (default) writes nothing and returns everything in memory.

width, height, dpi

Passed to ggplot2::ggsave() when outdir is supplied. Ignored otherwise.

...

Further arguments to DropletUtils::barcodeRanks(), such as exclude.from. Which others it accepts depends on the DropletUtils version – see DropletUtils versions.

multiplexed

Deprecated. The former name of multi; still accepted, with a warning.

Value

A named list with one element per run, each a list of:

data

Data frame of the plotted curve: barcode, rank, total and fitted, one row per distinct total, ordered by rank. fitted is NA throughout with DropletUtils 1.30 or later, which fits no spline. Zero-count barcodes are dropped (they have no place on a log axis) and ties are collapsed to one row, so this is far smaller than the raw matrix – small enough to write to CSV, which the full per-barcode table is not.

plot

A ggplot2 object, using theme_prepro(). Nothing is printed, so it can be assigned, modified with +, or saved.

knee, inflection

The two cutoffs, in UMIs.

n_barcodes

Total barcodes in the raw matrix, before any were dropped for plotting.

n_above_inflection

Barcodes at or above the inflection point – a rough expected cell count to compare against the filtered matrix.

h5

The raw H5 file the curve was computed from.

Runs whose raw matrix is missing, or whose curve barcodeRanks() cannot fit, are dropped from the manifest-mode result with a warning; in path mode either raises an error instead.

Details

This is the first plot to look at when a sample's cell count comes back unexpected. A sharp cliff between a plateau of high-count barcodes and a long tail of near-empty ones means cell calling had an easy decision to make. A shallow, gradual slope means it did not – usually ambient RNA, a low-viability sample, or a wetting failure – and the called cell count from that run should be treated with suspicion.

Reading the plot

Points

One per distinct total UMI count. Barcodes tying on total share a rank and plot at one position, so the curve is drawn from a few thousand points rather than the millions of barcodes behind it.

Fitted line

DropletUtils before 1.30 only: the smooth spline barcodeRanks() fits to the curve, whose derivatives give the knee and inflection. Undefined below lower, so it stops short of the right-hand tail. From 1.30, barcodeRanks() traces the curve directly and fits no spline, so no line is drawn – see DropletUtils versions.

Knee

Where the curve bends most sharply. The optimistic cutoff – barcodes above it are cells by any reading.

Inflection

Where the curve starts its final descent into the ambient tail. The permissive cutoff, and usually the closer of the two to what Cell Ranger actually called.

Neither line is a threshold this function applies. Nothing is filtered here; both are drawn so you can compare them against the cell count seuratFrom10x() returns from the same run's filtered matrix.

Memory

Raw matrices are large, and runs are processed strictly one at a time: each is read, ranked, reduced to its curve, and released before the next is touched. Peak memory is therefore set by the largest single run, not by the size of the manifest. rawMatrixFrom10x() is the function to reach for if you genuinely need the matrices themselves, and it makes no such promise.

DropletUtils versions

The installed DropletUtils is detected from what barcodeRanks() returns. Its method for finding the knee changed twice. Before 1.28 it fitted a smoothing spline and took derivatives; 1.28 switched to the point farthest from a line between plateau and inflection; 1.30 replaced both with a curve-tracing algorithm and stopped returning the spline. So the knee, and sometimes the inflection, can move between versions on the same data, and data$fitted is NA from 1.30 on. The arguments fit.bounds and df only do anything before 1.30; from 1.30 the ones that tune the fit are exclude.from, window and gradient.threshold.

See also

rawMatrixFrom10x() for the matrices this reads, DropletUtils::barcodeRanks() for the ranking itself, theme_prepro() for the theme.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# One run, in memory
ranks <- plotBarcodeRanks(path = "/path/to/Sample_1/outs", multi = FALSE)
ranks$Sample_1$plot
head(ranks$Sample_1$data)
ranks$Sample_1$knee

# Every run in a manifest, with CSVs and PNGs written out
manifest <- data.frame(
  Path  = c("/path/to/Sample_1/outs", "/path/to/Pool1/outs"),
  multi = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
ranks <- plotBarcodeRanks(manifest = manifest, outdir = "qc/barcode_ranks")

# Compare the expected cell count against what cell calling kept
vapply(ranks, function(x) x$n_above_inflection, numeric(1))

# The plots are plain ggplots
ranks[[1]]$plot + ggplot2::labs(subtitle = "Run 1, re-sequenced")

# One faceted figure across every run
curves <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(ranks), function(s) {
  cbind(Sample = s, ranks[[s]]$data)
}))
ggplot2::ggplot(curves, ggplot2::aes(rank, total, colour = Sample)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10() +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_prepro() +
  theme_prepro("airy")
} # }
